name: WildToolBench
description: WildToolBench is an LLM tool-use benchmark grounded in real-world user behavior patterns, designed to evaluate multi-turn, multi-step tool-use capabilities of large language models under complex, flexible, and messy user interactions. It focuses on challenges such as compositional tasks, implicit intent inference, and instruction transition in dialogue.
reputation: A relatively recent benchmark that is used in tool-use and agent-evaluation research, but it is not yet as established as older tool-use suites.
notes: No model achieves more than 15% accuracy, highlighting the challenge of real-world user behavior in LLM tool-use.
